key_insight: Graph grounding reduced hallucinations across all five evaluated LLMs, while general-purpose models generally outperformed domain-specific models on complex reasoning tasks.
clinical_relevance: Combining LLMs with structured biomedical knowledge may improve research tools, but this benchmark does not establish safety or effectiveness in patient care.
method: Benchmarked GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, and BioGPT.
Used DrugBank, NeuroSynth, Cognitive Atlas, Brain Map, and GDPKG.
Compared graph-grounded and graph-agnostic performance on multitier reasoning and factual-accuracy queries.
evidence_signal: Annotation agreement was substantial (Cohen’s κ = 0.781; Fleiss’ κ = 0.77), and model performance declined as query complexity increased.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical effect sizes for hallucination reduction and reports no clinical validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
